one_line: Maharaja of Tripura and pioneering royal photographer who modernized Agartala in the late 19th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, medium height, gently rounded build with a dignified posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a warm brown complexion, high cheekbones, neatly trimmed medium-length black moustache, small soul-patch beard, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes with a calm, observant gaze, default expression a composed half-smile suggesting quiet curiosity.
appearance.hair: Short, neatly combed black hair parted slightly to the right, mostly hidden under a white silk turban styled in late-19th-century princely fashion, with a modest gold turban band and a single small green gemstone at the front.
appearance.costume: He wears a cream-coloured, knee-length silk angarkha (cross-wrapped coat) with fine vertical jacquard stripes and subtle gold piping along the edges, fastened right-to-left with small cloth buttons, over a soft white cotton kurta visible at the collar and cuffs; his lower garment is a deep maroon silk dhoti with a broad gold border, pleated neatly and wrapped in the Bengali–Tripura style, falling to the ankles; a dark bottle-green velvet angavastram (shawl) with a thin gold woven edge is draped over his left shoulder and across his torso, signifying royal formality; he wears polished brown leather jutti-style shoes with slightly upturned toes, a narrow gold waist-belt with a simple rectangular buckle, and minimal jewellery: a single thin gold chain at the neck, a small round gold stud in each ear, and a plain gold ring on his right hand.
appearance.signature: A polished late-19th-century wooden field camera on a folding tripod, with a brass lens and a dark cloth focusing hood, which he holds by resting one hand on the camera body while the other lightly gathers the dark cloth, indicating active use.

ref_desc: Bir Chandra Manikya is a late-30s brown-complexioned Maharaja with an oval face, neat moustache, short black hair under a white silk turban, wearing a cream angarkha, maroon dhoti, green velvet shawl, brown jutti shoes, and carrying a wooden brass-lensed field camera on a tripod in cream, maroon, green, gold and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Bir Chandra Manikya: a dignified late-19th-century Maharaja in his late 30s with an oval brown face, high cheekbones, neat black moustache, small soul-patch beard and thoughtful almond-shaped eyes, short black hair mostly covered by a white silk turban with a modest gold band and a single small green gemstone front center; dress him in a cream knee-length silk angarkha with fine vertical jacquard stripes and subtle gold piping, worn over a white cotton kurta, paired with a deep maroon silk dhoti with a broad gold border wrapped to the ankles in Bengali–Tripura style, and a bottle-green velvet angavastram shawl with a thin gold edge draped over his left shoulder and across his torso, secured by a narrow gold waist-belt; put brown leather jutti-style shoes on his feet and add minimal jewellery, just a thin gold neck chain, small round gold ear studs and a plain gold ring on his right hand; his signature prop is a polished wooden late-19th-century field camera with a brass lens mounted on a folding tripod, one hand resting on the camera body and the other lightly holding the dark focusing cloth, all rendered in a restrained palette of cream, deep maroon, bottle green, gold and brown, with consistent detailing from multiple angles in a clean shonen-anime line style.
